The two shortest sections are at the top, so the top $50\%$ of the data are packed between $70$ and $80$.

$Q_1$**First quartile** (lower quartile)	The median of the lower half of the ordered data. About 25% of the data lies below it.
$Q_2$**Second quartile** (median)	The middle value of the ordered data. About 50% of the data lies below it.
$Q_3$**Third quartile** (upper quartile)	The median of the upper half of the ordered data. About 75% of the data lies below it.

1. $Q_2$: Find the median. It splits the ordered data into a lower half and an upper half. If the number of values is odd, exclude the median from both halves.
2. $Q_1$: Find the median of the lower half.
3. $Q_3$: Find the median of the upper half.

The **five-number summary** lists five values that describe a dataset, in order: the minimum, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ (the median), $Q_3$ and the maximum.

**Five-number summary**
Min	$Q_1$	$Q_2$	$Q_3$	Max

**Outliers** are values far above or below the rest of the data. They greatly affect the range and standard deviation.

The **interquartile range** (IQR) is the distance between $Q_3$ and $Q_1$. It is the spread of the middle half of the data.

It measures spread with less impact from outliers.
A **box plot** shows the five-number summary on a number line. The box runs from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$, a line inside it marks the median ($Q_2$), and whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum.
The quartiles divide a box plot into four parts: the left whisker, the two halves of the box and the right whisker. Each part contains about 25% of the data, whatever its length.

Side-by-side box plots on the same scale make it easy to compare two datasets.

A higher median means a higher typical value. Whether a higher or lower value is better depends on the context.

A smaller IQR means the middle 50% of values lie closer together, so the data are more **consistent**.

The whiskers of a box plot show the shape of the distribution. A longer left whisker means a tail to the left (negatively skewed). A longer right whisker means a tail to the right (positively skewed). Whiskers of similar length with the median near the centre of the box mean the distribution is symmetrical.

A data value is an **outlier** if it is below the **lower fence**, $Q_1-1.5\times IQR$, or above the **upper fence**, $Q_3+1.5\times IQR$. The fences are also called the lower and upper limits. Values exactly on a fence are not outliers.
